correctness.rationale: For the corrected finding, reconstructed the curvature-risk normalization from Böröczky–Reitzner and the Hölder lower bound with equality at rho proportional to (lambda f^p+(1-lambda)g^p)^(1/p). Strict concavity for unequal laws gives an interior stationary multiplier and equalizes the actual two risks, establishing a matching upper bound within the admissible positive continuous densities. For the oval, r=h+h''=1+t cos(2 theta), dS=r dtheta and curvature=1/r; p=3. Independently set x=t cos(2 theta), U=<r^(2/3)>^(-3), V=<r^(1/3)>^(-3), and factor the half-weight denominator S=(U+V)/2 times (1+Ux/(U+V)). U/(U+V)=1/2+O(t^4). The angular factor (1+x)^(1/3)(1+x/2)^(-2/3)=1-x²/12+x³/12+O(x^4). U-V=-t^4/72+O(t^6), so the slope coefficient is ((3/8)/12-1/72)/3=5/864, with the second derivative -t²/9+O(t^4) from <x²>=t²/2. Even analytic dependence and the simple zero of H'/t² yield the shift 5t²/96+O(t^4). Taylor expansion gives gain 25t^6/165888+O(t^8) in H; cubing multiplies the leading coefficient by three. No finite checker proves the expansion. Replay is the exact calculation in the repair; inspected the frozen verifier and its verification notes without running the script. The claim applies to fixed-density leading errors and sufficiently small nonzero t, not finite N or general shape perturbations.
